name: Huang T’ing-chien
bio: Huang T’ing-chien was a poet and calligrapher of the Sung dynasty. His poem here is set at the festival of the tombs.
The poems here are Herbert A. Giles’s versions in Chinese Poetry in English Verse (1898), given with the poet’s name as spelled in that book.

poems.title: Annual Worship at Tombs
poems.author: Huang T’ing-chien
poems.text:
The peach and plum trees smile with flowers this famous day of spring,
And country graveyards round about with lamentations ring.
Thunder has startled insect life and roused the gnats and bees,
A gentle rain has urged the crops and soothed the flowers and trees —
Perhaps on this side lie the bones of a wretch whom no one knows;
On that, the sacred ashes of a patriot repose.
But who across the centuries can hope to mark each spot
Where fool or hero, joined in death, beneath the brambles rot?

poems.title: 清明 (Qing ming)
poems.author: Huang T’ing-chien
poems.collection: 千家詩 (Poems of a Thousand Poets)
poems.text:
佳節清明桃李笑，野田荒冢只生愁。
雷驚天地龍蛇蟄，雨足郊原草木柔。
人乞祭餘驕妾婦，士甘焚死不公侯。
賢愚千載知誰是，滿眼蓬蒿共一丘。
